newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end mixed in heavy trading.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end mixed in heavy trading.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended mixed on Tuesday in brisk turnover as shares in embattled gold prospector Bre-X Minerals Ltd. resumed trading and lost nearly all their value.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index fell 20.76 points to finish at 6129.96 after its second heaviest trading session ever.
But the broader market was mixed with gaining issues outnumbering declines 508 to 484. Another 281 issues ended flat.
Fred Ketchen, ScotiaMcLeod's director of trading, said investors decided to sell and reap profits after a six-day winning streak.
"It was a mixed bag and I think we have a market that is still headed higher but every once in a while, finds it prudent to lock in profits," Ketchen said.
Volume totalled 149.2 million shares worth C$1.4 billion ($1.02 billion).
Trading in Bre-X resumed on Tuesday after Monday's all-day halt following a report that revealed its Busang gold find was a fraud instead of the world's largest gold discovery.

The Calgary-based prospector -- once worth C$6 billion ($4.4 billion) -- sank C$3.145 to close at C8.5 cents in panic selling of 58.3 million shares. It was the biggest one-day volume of a single stock in the TSE's history.
The previous one-day record was set by Black Swan Gold Mines Ltd. with 38.5 million shares on April 16, 1996.
Discount brokers said they were receiving requests for Bre-X stock certificates from souvenir seekers.
Of Toronto's 14 sub-indices, 10 lost ground, including transportation, consumer products and golds. Four rose led by conglomerates and media.
Other active issues included Norcen Energy Resources Ltd. which rose 1.85 to 30.60 after making an all-cash $303 million bid for Basic Petroleum International Ltd.
